declarations.docstring: A finite-dimensional semisimple algebra over an algebraically closed field is equivalent to a finite product of nonzero-size full matrix algebras.
The third auxiliary ideal of the tensor product is two-sided.
The first auxiliary ideal of the tensor product is nilpotent when the left factor is finite-dimensional.
The second auxiliary ideal of the tensor product is nilpotent when the right factor is finite-dimensional.
The third auxiliary ideal of the tensor product is nilpotent when both factors are finite-dimensional.
The tensor product of two finite-dimensional semisimple algebras over an algebraically closed field is semisimple.
If the tensor product of the Jacobson-radical quotients is semisimple, the Jacobson radical of the tensor product is contained in the third auxiliary ideal.
For finite-dimensional algebras over an algebraically closed field, the Jacobson radical of their tensor product equals the third auxiliary ideal.

For two algebra actions on a finite-dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field, the Jacobson radical of the tensor product of their ranges equals the corresponding third auxiliary ideal.
Every nilpotent ideal of a ring is contained in its Jacobson radical.
The product of two ideals mapped through the left tensor-product inclusion is contained in the image of their product.
A power of an ideal mapped through the left tensor-product inclusion is contained in the image of the corresponding ideal power.
The product of two ideals mapped through the right tensor-product inclusion is contained in the image of their product.
A power of an ideal mapped through the right tensor-product inclusion is contained in the image of the corresponding ideal power.
The quotient of a finite-dimensional tensor-product algebra by its Jacobson radical is algebra-equivalent to the tensor product of the two Jacobson-radical quotients.
The quotient by the third auxiliary tensor-product ideal is algebra-equivalent to the tensor product of the factor algebras modulo their Jacobson radicals.
A first auxiliary ideal of a tensor-product algebra.
A second auxiliary ideal of a tensor-product algebra.
A third auxiliary ideal of a tensor-product algebra.
The third auxiliary tensor-product ideal is the kernel of the map to the tensor product of the Jacobson-radical quotients.
For finite-dimensional factor algebras, the third auxiliary tensor-product ideal is contained in the Jacobson radical of the tensor product.
The module structure induced by two commuting algebra actions over the tensor product of their ranges.
The algebra homomorphism from the tensor product of the ranges of two commuting actions to endomorphisms of their common module.
On a pure tensor from the two action ranges, the tensor-product action is the product of the corresponding endomorphisms.
The algebra homomorphism from a tensor product to the tensor product of the two factor algebras modulo their Jacobson radicals.
The tensor-product map to the tensor product of the Jacobson-radical quotients is surjective.
The tensor-product quotient map sends a pure tensor to the pure tensor of the two quotient classes.
